aspects.says: Composition with one lock costs a method for every operation callers need and serializes readers that a CopyOnWriteArrayList let run without a lock.
basis: section:A Class That Owns the State and the Lock Doesn't Depend on What It Wraps
aspects.reason: a cost the page states from the code shown; no deterministic test can grade a reader on it

aspects.says: A class that keeps the collection private and runs every read and write under its own lock makes a compound action atomic whatever the inner collection is.
basis: section:A Class That Owns the State and the Lock Doesn't Depend on What It Wraps

aspects.says: The composed class's guarantee holds only while no reference to its state escapes: a list stored from the caller, or returned by a getter, is a path around the lock.
basis: section:A Class That Owns the State and the Lock Doesn't Depend on What It Wraps

aspects.says: A race in a subclass's compound action can stay invisible under load (0 to 84 duplicates in five runs), while a forced interleaving between the check and the act shows it every time.
basis: section:A Subclass's synchronized Method Excludes Only Code That Locks this
aspects.reason: it is a claim about how races are found, shown by the page's two runs; the practices use forced interleavings themselves rather than grade the reader on choosing one

aspects.says: A helper's synchronized method locks the helper, so helpers created per request or per tenant over one shared collection exclude nothing; the helper must take the lock the collection itself takes, which works only where the collection documents it, as Collections.synchronizedList does.
basis: section:A Helper Outside the Class Must Take the Lock the Class Takes

aspects.says: putIfAbsent receives a value already built, so its construction runs on every call; computeIfAbsent runs its function only when the key is absent, once per call.
basis: section:putIfAbsent Builds the Value Before It Knows It Is Needed

aspects.says: A synchronized method added by a subclass locks this, so it excludes only code that locks this; over a base that locks a private object, such as CopyOnWriteArrayList or ConcurrentHashMap, the base's own methods run straight through it.
basis: section:A Subclass's synchronized Method Excludes Only Code That Locks this

aspects.says: When the class already offers the compound action (addIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent, remove(key, value)), calling it is atomic against the class's own methods; get-then-put on a ConcurrentHashMap hands some callers different values.
basis: section:When the Class Already Has the Compound Action, Call It
